title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page computes, by generators and relations, the divided-power (PD) algebra generated by one element λ over a ring A. This is the local algebra behind PD envelopes in crystalline / de Rham cohomology.

(1) Grothendieck takes the polynomial algebra A[Γ^n(λ), n ≥ 1] and imposes two families of relations.
- (*) Γ^m(λ)Γ^n(λ) = ((m+n)!/(m!n!)) Γ^{m+n}(λ).
- (**) (x^n − y^n)Γ^n(λ) = 0 for all x, y in A with (x−y)λ = 0.
In modern terms the quotient is Roby's Γ_A(M) for the cyclic module M = Aλ ≅ A/Ann(λ).

(2) The NB explains the role of (**). It makes the definition Γ^n(λx) := x^nΓ^n(λ) independent of the representative: if λx = λy then x^nΓ^n(λ) ≡ y^nΓ^n(λ). The remaining axioms of a divided-power structure then follow.
- The addition formula Γ^n(λ(x+y)) = Σ Γ^i(λx)Γ^{n−i}(λy) follows from (*).
- Γ^n(xy) ≡ x^nΓ^n(y) is trivial.
- Products such as Γ^n(λx)Γ^m(λy) are handled similarly.
For y = 0, (**) gives x^nΓ^n(λ) = 0 for x in Ann(λ), as it must.

(3) Next Grothendieck supposes that a prime p is nilpotent in A. Then every integer prime to p is a unit in A. Writing n = Σ a_ν p^ν in base p, Γ^n(λ) equals a unit times ∏_ν Γ^{p^ν}(λ)^{a_ν}. So the same algebra is the quotient of A[(Γ^{p^ν}(λ))_{ν≥0}] by the same two families, with Γ^n defined from the Γ^{p^ν} as above.

(4) He then conjectures ('semble-t-il') that the multiplicativity relations (*) reduce to the boxed relations Γ^{p^ν}(λ)^p = ((p^{ν+1})!/(p^ν!)^p) Γ^{p^{ν+1}}(λ). The coefficient is p times a p-adic unit, since v_p((p^{ν+1})!) − p·v_p(p^ν!) = 1. So the algebra is A[x_0, x_1, …]/(x_ν^p − p·u_ν·x_{ν+1}, plus the annihilator relations).

(5) The last lines start checking this with exponents e = p + a, 0 ≤ a ≤ p−1, to see how Γ^{p^ν}(λ)^e reduces; the page breaks off there.

This is the standard structure theorem for the divided-power polynomial algebra over Z_(p). It is needed to describe PD envelopes locally and to see their non-noetherian, p-torsion behaviour.

The neighbouring transcriptions concern quasi-functions and heights on abelian varieties. They seem to come from a different document misfiled in the scan, so they give no context.
errors: No mathematical error. The reduction of (*) to the boxed p-power relations is stated tentatively ('semble-t-il') and not proved on the page. It is true once one also uses that the units Γ^n/∏(Γ^{p^ν})^{a_ν} are compatible, which is standard.

The final lines ('pour p ≤ e < 2p−1, donc pour e = p+a (0 ≤ a ≤ p−1)') are an unfinished check and are partly illegible; the indexing starts at ν ≥ 1 in the note although ν ≥ 0, i.e. Γ^1 = λ itself, is needed.

ideas.what: Presentation of the divided-power algebra on a cyclic module A/Ann(λ) by generators Γ^n(λ) and relations (multiplicativity plus (x^n−y^n)Γ^n(λ) = 0 when (x−y)λ = 0)
ideas.modern_name: Roby's divided power algebra Γ_A(M) for M = A/I
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963–65); used by Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Roby, 'Lois polynômes et lois formelles…' (1963); Berthelot SLN 407; Berthelot–Ogus

ideas.what: When p is nilpotent, Γ is generated by the Γ^{p^ν}(λ), with relations Γ^{p^ν}^p = ((p^{ν+1})!/(p^ν!)^p) Γ^{p^{ν+1}}, the coefficient being p·unit
ideas.modern_name: Structure of divided power polynomial algebras over Z_(p) / PD envelopes: Z_(p)[x_0, x_1, …]/(x_ν^p − p u_ν x_{ν+1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; Berthelot's thesis; Berthelot–Ogus 'Notes on crystalline cohomology'
ideas.where_published: Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (1974), ch. I; Berthelot–Ogus (1978) §3

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working-out of the local structure of divided-power algebras, in the period when Grothendieck and Berthelot were setting up crystalline cohomology. All of it is standard (Roby, Berthelot). It is of mild historical interest only as evidence that Grothendieck computed these presentations himself.
transcription_corrections: Line after NB: 'qui a un sens en effet puisque grâce à (**) λx = λy implique x^nΓ^n(λ) ≡ y^nΓ^n(λ)'. The 'grâce à (**)' is an insertion above the line.
'Si maintenant dans A un premier p est nilpotent, on trouve aussi le quotient de A[(Γ^{p^ν}(λ))_{ν≥1}] par les relations', rather than 'dans un premier ≠ p … est nilp.'
'les relations Γ^n(λ(x+y)) ≡ … résultent alors des (*), Γ^n(xy) ≡ x^nΓ^n(y) est trivial, ainsi que Γ^n(λx)Γ^m(λy) = …'
Boxed formula: Γ^{p^ν}(λ)^p = ((p^{ν+1})!/(p^ν!)^p) Γ^{p^{ν+1}}(λ). A crossed-out earlier attempt precedes the fraction.
'Les premières relations se réduisent, semble-t-il, à' (not 'se ré[?]duisent').
Archive page number is 34. The neighbouring 'previous/next page' transcriptions (pages 33/35 of a typed text on quasi-functions and heights) appear to belong to a different document.
